Independent finite replay: for p=2,3 in dimension two, separate supports of affine spans of dimension 0, 1, 2. Enumerated affine subset orbits by the two coordinate translations, coordinate swap, a shear and one-coordinate sign change. The nonempty subset class counts by size are [1,1,1,1] and [1,1,2,2,2,2,1,1,1]. Singleton supports give that histogram for their fibers; line supports of ℓ=2,…,p give multisets of ℓ quotient subset sizes from {1,…,p}, weighted by p times their sum (line stabilizer induces all permutations of a support in these cases). Full-span supports use the affine subset histogram after removing singletons, pairs and the line-triple class at p=3, with sizes multiplied by p². This reproduces every coefficient in examples.json for both extensions, totaling 9 and 39. Labeled split by span dimension gives 60+54+5=119 and 4599+5880+454=10933. Direct affine subset orbits in prime dimensions f=1 also give the four claimed totals.
correctness.rationale: The right translations generate inner orbits equal to the rows. Every automorphism thus has row maps F_b and a common base permutation h, satisfying F_b(a+t)−F_b(a)=h(b)−h(b−t) for every a,t. This difference is additive in t and is a bijective slope. Expressing the same h through each row shows all slopes equal one F_p-linear L, with h(b)=L(b)+v. Conversely these maps with arbitrary independent u(b)=F_b(0) preserve the operation. For a fixed support B, differences b−d for any one b generate all differences of B; finite closure is therefore equivalent to every nonempty fiber being a union of W_B-cosets. Quotient first by the normal group of independent u(b)-translations. Each row now independently carries a nonempty subset of V/W_B up to translations; its size in Q is |W_B| times its size in the quotient. The residual affine group moves the rows and acts by the corresponding induced L on the labels. Closing an h-cycle of length ℓ requires the initial translation-orbit to be fixed by the induced L^ℓ. For any such fixed translation-orbit O in a quotient H, each of its |O| representatives has exactly |H|/|O| translating vectors bringing its image under M back to itself. Thus its contribution to the average in (1) is exactly one, including nonfree translation-orbits; nonfixed orbits contribute zero. Fixed subsets of each affine bijection are exactly cycle unions. Weighted Burnside then yields (2), including W_B=V where the nonempty zero-space subset contributes a single monomial. For f=1 a singleton row support gives the full affine subset action on its fiber, while all supports of size ≥2 have full rows and give affine support orbits. Counting translations and the multipliers of each order yields (4)–(5) and the identity-term asymptotic. The argument uses the additive F_p-space and applies in characteristic two.
residual_risks: The finite replay covers only the stated small examples; the general result uses the proof. Rank one refers to a realization over a degree-f extension field, not rank one over F_p when f>1. No multiplicative field structure, formal verification, or complexity bound is assumed.

value.rationale: This counts the full natural embedded population modulo its actual symmetries, not only labeled subsets, retraction images, or abstract types. The quotient-space factors make the computation much smaller than direct Burnside on the full automorphism group, expose when equal-size labeled results have distinct ambient types, and give both a prime-field asymptotic and reproducible nontrivial extension examples.
residual_risks: Exact finite algorithm, not a large-f complexity guarantee or a classification of arbitrary Alexander modules.
